hypothesis: A prompt chunk's compressor and indexer-compressor projections (four bf16 matrices on a ratio-4 layer, 2,560 rows x 4,096 over 128 tokens) run one launch per matrix whose blocks reduce every output through shared memory: about 0.7 ms of kernel time per chunk and layer, most of it the reduction rather than the multiply-adds. Computing every matrix in one register-tiled launch that keeps the old kernels' arithmetic exactly (each output's 256 fma chains in the same column order, added by the same fixed tree: three levels in registers, five by warp shuffles) gives the same bits in about a quarter of the kernel time and shortens the time to the first token.
model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 architecture, abliterated weights (same shapes), safetensors, native FP8/FP4
command: make -C c -f Makefile.deepseek-v4 deepseek-v4 CUDA=1 DEEPGEMM=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.3 ARCH=native; deepseek_v4 <model> --prompt-file prompt3k.txt --max-tokens 36 --memory-gb 16 with the environment in config; the arms alternate (baseline, trial) three times on one binary; tok_s = 3278 prompt tokens / time_to_first_token from the engine's `timing` line (prompt throughput)

hardware.storage: Samsung 990 PRO 4TB + 980 PRO 2TB NVMe in one LVM volume, ext4, direct aligned reads
